IN THE COURT OF APPEALS OF THE STATE OF OREGON
State of Oregon,
Plaintiff-Respondent,
v.
Jeff Kelvin Yocom,
Defendant-Appellant.
Washington County Circuit Court No. 23CR21349
Court of Appeals No. A186155
ORDER REVERSING IN PART; APPELLATE JUDGMENT
Before Egan, Presiding Judge, and Joyce, Judge.
The parties jointly move under ORAP 10.35 to reverse the parts of the trial
court’s judgment that require defendant to pay per diem fees.1
The parties agree that the trial court committed reversible error by requiring
defendant to pay per diem fees without pronouncing those terms in defendant’s
presence, and that the appeal does not present a substantial question of law. See, e.g.,
State v. Sankey, 289 Or App 846, 847, 409 P3d 73 (2018). The parties further agree on
the disposition of the appeal and that a published opinion deciding the appeal would not
benefit the bench or the bar. The court agrees with the parties’ identification of error
and that summary disposition is appropriate in this case. The motion is granted.
Portion of judgment requiring defendant to pay per diem fees reversed; otherwise
affirmed.
James C. Egan
Presiding Judge
4/3/2026
1 A copy of the parties’ motion, for the trial court’s review, is available on the
court’s Appellate Case Management System (ACMS).
